xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: National Stock Exchange of India Limited ("NSE")
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: Imposition of fine of Rs.11800 /- (Including GST) by NSE
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Non-compliance with Regulation 31(1) (b) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: There is no material impact on the Company’s financial position, operations, or any other activities.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Joint Commissioner of CGST, Pune – I Commissionerate, Pune
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The order was passed disallowing TRAN-1 credit under Section 73 of the CGST Act 2017 to pay tax of Rs.3,15,63,781/- along with penalty of Rs.31,56,378/- under Section 122(2) and interest as applicable under Section 50(3)of the CGST Act 2017.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The matter relating to disallowance of ISD credit transferred through TRAN‑1 was earlier disputed before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court, which remanded it back to the jurisdictional officer.The company subsequently filed a follow‑up letter with the officer and, based on its assessment and prevailing law, reasonably expected a favorable outcome with no material impact on its financial position, operations, or other activities. The proceedings have now been conclusively resolved, as the Joint Commissioner of CGST, Pune II Commissionerate has dropped the demand order (Order No. ZD2712250096877 dated 02‑12‑2025), an outcome favorable for FIL.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Joint Commissioner of CGST, Pune – I Commissionerate, Pune
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The order was passed for the tax demand of Rs.1,25,29,080/- (which was already paid by the Company and appropriated against the demand) and levied a penalty of Rs.12,52,908/- under Section 73(9) and interest of Rs.26,56,851/- under Section 50 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act, 2017).
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company is in the process of availing the amnesty scheme for interest and penalty. Based on its assessment and the prevailing legal framework, the Company reasonably expects a favorable outcome. Accordingly, there is no material impact on the financial position, operations, or other activities of the Company. The said case has now been closed. Order for closure of proceedings has been received. (Ref. No. ZD270725097319R dated 22-07-2025)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Assistant Commissioner of CGST, Division – II, Vadodara – I
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The order was passed for the tax demand of Rs.29,488 /- (Rupees Twenty Nine Thousand Four Hundred and Eighty Eight Only) along with applicable interest under Section 73(9) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act, 2017) and levied a penalty of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) under the provision of Section 122(2)(a) read with Section 73(1) of the State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (SGST Act, 2017) and Integrated Goods and Services Tax
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has paid the tax dues and filed an application under amenesty scheme for interest and penalty. The said case has now been closed. Order for closure of proceedings has been received. (Ref. No: ZD240325105467L dated 27-03-2025)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Office of the Commissioner of Central GST, Kolhapur, Maharashtra

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER STATE TAX CIRCLE-13, INDORE
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The order has been passed for a tax demand of ₹14,112/-, along with interest of ₹17,774/- and a penalty of ₹14,112/- under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act, 2017). Reason: The demand has arisen due to the duplicate generation of an e-way bill for a single invoice.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has decided to settle the liability arising from the order, comprising tax of ₹14,112/‑, interest of ₹17,774/‑, and penalty of ₹14,112/‑, as this approach ensures compliance, prevents escalation of costs, and enables timely closure of the matter.
